_comment: 2. Two arms are given the same two actions against the same notebook, at
the same moment. Nothing sequences them: the one with less ground to
cover arrives first and takes it, and the other is refused
OBJECT_CLAIMED and told who has it.
The two plans are identical. The whole difference is the walk, measured on
this layout and seed:
ridgeback_1  spawn (2.44, 7.98)  ->  7.7 m,  77 travel ticks, arrives 78
ridgeback_2  spawn (2.44, 8.63)  ->  9.0 m,  90 travel ticks, arrives 91
so ridgeback_1 grasps at 79 and ridgeback_2 reaches for it at 92. The 13
ticks come from both the spawn offset and the pose each sampler drew in
the annulus, and they are deterministic for a fixed seed -- but they are
only 13 ticks. A shared spawn (every S1 layout is one: all nine robots
start within about a metre of each other) is what keeps the margin that
narrow.
ridgeback_2 is standing in reach of the notebook when it is refused, and
that is the point: the refusal is not about where it is. _grasp checks in
the order arm -> may-lift -> already-held -> UNCLAIMED -> near
(symbolic_contention._grasp), so a robot that walked all the way there is
told the thing is taken rather than how far away it is.
Run with coop2/team_layouts/s1/sets_3.json (9 robots) on v4_s1_v4_lh.
Expect:
ridgeback_1  grasp(notebook.n.01_1)  -> success
ridgeback_2  grasp(notebook.n.01_1)  -> PRE_CONDITION_ERROR:
notebook.n.01_1 is currently held by ridgeback_1, so you cannot grasp
it. Pick a different target, or ask them to release it.
